# Data

The data regarding animal product intake was sourced through kaggle.com @R-data, while information regarding GDP was sourced from worldometers.info @R-GDP. Each group contains 20 observations, each sampled from a bigger sample of 76 observations from the animal group, and 76 from the plant. The variable of GDP was divided by 1 billion, meaning that all interpretations will be in billions of dollars. The separation between the two groups is `r val`% in animal product fat intake.

The following table shows basic summary statistics for each group in billions of dollars.

## Exploratory Data Analysis

### EDA 1

```{r EDA histogram, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.cap = 'Histograms of Animal and Plant distributions showing GDP in billions', out.width = '50%', fig.align = 'center'}


```
### EDA 2


```{r EDA Equal Variance, echo = FALSE}
ftest <- var.test(value ~ group, plot.data,
         alternative = "two.sided")
```



```{r, boxplot, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.cap = 'Boxplot comparison of the distribution between Plant and Animal Groups by GDP in billions', out.width = '50%', fig.align = 'center'}

ggplot(data = plot.data, mapping = aes(x = group, y = value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ylab("GDP") +
  ylim(0, 2700) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

```

In order to perform any testing with normal theory, a transformation must be performed on both groups in order to move forward with the normality assumption.s

The following histograms show the relatively normal distribution of both groups after a log transformation, which are both common transformations for right tailed distributions.

```{r, transformed histograms ftest, fig.cap = 'Histograms of Animal and Plant distributions showing Log(GDP)', echo = FALSE}

```

# Summary of Conclusions


# Future Recommendations

After completing this analysis, it is recognized that there is the possibility of confounding in this study. A recommendation on further analysis would be to find a way to include variables that would limit such confounding. Another recommendation would be to increase the sample size of the study, considering a larger sample size would greatly increase the accuracy of all tests performed.

This analysis has also sparked my interest in analyzing the health benefits of a vegan oriented diet. It is recommended that a future study be completed comparing the same independent variable with a different dependent variable measuring some health outcome, such as the percentage of those with cardiovascular diseases, or percentage of deaths by Covid-19.
